record.original_question: For triangular forests, and in particular for equilateral triangles, what guaranteed-escape curve minimizes the worst-case escape time for a hiker who knows the forest's shape but not the starting point or initial direction?

evidence.quote: The problem is still open for very simple choices of F.
The problems remains unsolved for triangles. There is a conjecture for the best curve for equilateral triangles in [3].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Bellman's lost-in-a-forest problem. Let F be a closed convex region in the plane (the "forest"). A "hiker" starts at an unknown point p in the interior of F facing an unknown direction θ ∈ [0, 2π). The hiker travels along a planar curve γ (a rectifiable path beginning at the origin in a coordinate system attached to the hiker's initial position and heading) and "escapes" once the path reaches the boundary ∂F. A curve γ is called a guaranteed-escape path for F if, for every starting point p ∈ F and every initial direction θ, the rigid motion of γ determined by (p, θ) meets ∂F at some finite arc length t(γ, p, θ); the worst-case escape length is

  L(γ, F) = sup_{p∈F, θ∈[0,2π)} t(γ, p, θ).

The problem: determine a curve γ* minimizing L(γ, F) over all guaranteed-escape paths, in the following two cases:
(a) F is an arbitrary triangle (the "triangular forest" case);
(b) F is an equilateral triangle of fixed side length.

In each case, find the optimal worst-case escape length L(γ*, F) and exhibit an optimal curve γ*.
artifact.status_search_result: The shortest guaranteed-escape path for a general triangular forest, and specifically for an equilateral triangle, is not known. Conjectured optimal curves (e.g., three-segment zigzag paths of Besicovitch type) appear in the literature, and recent preprints propose general constructions, but no proof of optimality has been established. The problem is broadly described as still open.

status_evidence.title: Bellman's lost-in-a-forest problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The shortest escape path is not known in the case of an equilateral triangular region.
status_evidence.claim: The optimal escape path for an equilateral triangular forest is unknown.

status_evidence.title: A General Solution to Bellman's Lost-in-a-forest Problem
status_evidence.snippet: For convex polygonal forests, the escape path is constructed piecewise of line segments and circular arcs; conjectures exist for triangles.
status_evidence.claim: Only conjectural optimal paths are known for triangular forests.
